title: How We Got LLMs to Recommend Our Open Source Library — Christopher Burns, Inth
talk_summary: A founder of an open-source cookie-banner library describes a 'docs pipeline' (Lead Type) that generates agent-facing artifacts—hand-written llms.txt, llms-full.txt, per-page .md twins, and markdown bundled into node_modules with an agents.md—so coding agents find and use the library without web search. He cites ~50% token savings from bundling docs in node_modules and claims LLM recommendations became their #1 inbound source.

takeaways.technique: Bundle docs into the package/repo as agents.md + markdown
takeaways.what_they_do: Ship the bundled markdown docs inside node_modules with an agents.md pointing agents to them, so agents read local docs instead of searching the web or inferring from compiled source.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we take the bundled markdown documents and then we also put them in the node modules with an agents.md file

takeaways.what_they_do: Write a ~40-line curated index by hand rather than auto-generating a huge one, mapping questions to the right pages.
takeaways.evidence_quote: For about 40 good lines beats 1,000 lines of noise from our testing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose three tools—search docs, get page, ask docs—over the docs corpus so agents can query instead of crawling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our tool is already uh um exposing three different tools to WebMCP. Search docs, get pages, and ask docs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use external harnesses (Cloudflare's, aura.ai) to score how well agents can consume the site/docs, and track the score over time as the space changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there was not really any like test suites yet, or test harnesses, on like is your site agent ready?

takeaways.technique: Serve markdown twins instead of HTML
takeaways.what_they_do: Provide a .md version of every page plus content negotiation (Accept header) and a ?mode=agent query fallback so agents get markdown, not HTML.
takeaways.evidence_quote: HTML is expensive, and why can't we just ship markdown to the agents?

takeaways.technique: Skills that force reading local docs and verifying versions
takeaways.what_they_do: Add a skill/instruction telling agents to read the bundled docs and verify they match the installed version before answering.
takeaways.evidence_quote: read the bundles and verify that they match and go from there
